title: Serving Large Language Models on Huawei CloudMatrix384
technique: CloudMatrix-Infer: PDC-disaggregated (prefill/decode/caching) serving of DeepSeek-R1 on a 384-NPU UB-interconnect supernode with EP320 decode, microbatch pipelining, INT8, MTP, EMS context caching

optimized_metrics.evidence: sustained throughput, while meeting tight service-level latency objectives under dynamic, heterogeneous real-world conditions
We assess absolute decode throughput (tokens/s) targeting a time-per-output-token (TPOT) SLO of below 50 ms
a tailored microbatch-based decode pipeline for CloudMatrix384 that maximizes resource utilization and reduces execution latency

headline_claim.text: CloudMatrix-Infer delivers a prefill throughput of 6,688 tokens/s per NPU, and a decode throughput of 1,943 tokens/s per NPU (at <50 ms TPOT)... sustaining a decode throughput of 538 tokens/s per NPU even under the stricter sub-15 ms TPOT constraint.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: We assess absolute decode throughput (tokens/s) targeting a time-per-output-token (TPOT) SLO of below 50 ms, and also evaluate throughput normalized by the accelerator's computer power (tokens/s per TFLOPS) as an indicator of compute efficiency.
metric_definitions.notes: Per-accelerator (NPU, i.e. per die/chip as in tables), per-decode-phase; output tokens at fixed batch size (96 per NPU) and KV length 4096; the TPOT bound is met by choosing the batch size (Table 4: batch 96/24/8 for 50/30/15 ms SLO). Effective MTP acceptance rate of 70% assumed for single speculative token. No formal definition of TPOT given; Table 3 reports 'Achieved TPOT (ms)' per decode step (e.g. 49.4).

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Under a relaxed SLO of 50 ms, CloudMatrix-Infer supports a batch size of 96 and achieves a throughput of 1,943 tokens/s per NPU while satisfying the latency constraint. As the SLO tightens to 30 ms and 15 ms, the batch sizes reduce to 24 and 8 respectively, resulting in lower throughputs of 974 and 538 tokens/s per NPU.
metric_definitions.notes: TPOT-constrained throughput = max per-NPU decode tokens/s with batch size tuned so achieved TPOT <= SLO (achieved 49.4/24.6/14.9 ms). Measured under steady-state fixed batch, not request-rate sweep.

metric_definitions.notes: Input (prompt) tokens/s per accelerator; batch size 16,384 tokens; default 5,655 vs 'Perfect EPLB' (idealized, projected) 6,688.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: throughput normalized by the accelerator's computer power (tokens/s per TFLOPS) as an indicator of compute efficiency
metric_definitions.notes: Hardware-normalized throughput; used to compare against H800/H100 numbers.

slo_spec: TPOT SLO of 50 ms (also 30 ms and 15 ms) in decode; batch size tuned per SLO; no percentile specified; latency SLOs mentioned qualitatively for PDC node ratio adaptation.
load_regime: fixed batch size per phase (decode batch 96/NPU at 4K KV; prefill 16K-token batches); no request-rate sweep
tradeoff_acknowledged: Throughput-latency: decode throughput falls from 1,943 to 974 to 538 tokens/s per NPU as TPOT SLO tightens from 50 to 30 to 15 ms (batch 96->24->8). MTP raises per-iteration latency but improves overall throughput (§6).
hardware: Huawei CloudMatrix384 (384 Ascend 910 NPUs, 192 Kunpeng CPUs, UB network)
workloads: synthetic prompt/KV lengths (1K-4K); comparisons with published DeepSeek H800 and SGLang H100 numbers
extractor_notes: Industrial system paper. TPOT never formally defined; used as per-step decode latency. Baseline comparisons are against published numbers (different batch sizes: 128 vs 96) so TPOT-constrained throughput is not exactly iso-batch. Prefill 'Perfect EPLB' numbers are idealized projections.
